mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates the Federal Reserve is easing policy, which lowers discount rates and increases the present value of expected equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of macro easing episodes, or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the pre-easing period mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals tightening monetary policy, which raises the opportunity cost of capital and compresses discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 60% of tightening episodes, or 60-day returns are not statistically lower than the pre-tightening period mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 5,000 over three months indicates weakening labor demand, which reduces corporate hiring and future earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of labor demand weakening episodes, or 20-day returns are not statistically lower than the pre-weakening period mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) below 3,000 over three months indicates strengthening labor demand, which boosts hiring and future earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day forward returns in > 60% of labor demand strengthening episodes, or 60-day returns are not statistically higher than the pre-strengthening period mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 2% over three months indicates robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings growth and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of robust consumer demand episodes, or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the pre-demand episode mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% over three months indicates weakening supply capacity, which reduces future earnings growth and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 60% of supply capacity weakening episodes, or 60-day returns are not statistically lower than the pre-weakening period mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% over three months indicates strong labor market conditions, which increases equity risk appetite and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of strong labor market episodes, or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than the pre-strong-labor-market period mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% over three months indicates accelerating inflation, which compresses discount rates and reduces future earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 60% of accelerating inflation episodes, or 60-day returns are not statistically lower than the pre-accelerating-inflation period mean (p > 0.05).
